name: Veneers / Turkey teeth

lead: Veneers are thin shells of porcelain or composite resin bonded to the front of teeth to change colour, shape or apparent alignment. The payoff people want is a uniform, brighter, straighter-looking smile. Multi-tooth makeovers are called Hollywood smile treatments, and Turkey teeth is a nickname for veneers or crowns from low-cost dental clinics in Turkey.

A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of 29 studies reported pooled survival of about 96% for feldspathic, 94% for leucite-reinforced and 97% for lithium disilicate veneers at around 10 years. A 2024 narrative review found similar survival, with dentin exposure lowering success. On looksmaxxing forums veneers are described as a high-impact change to facial appearance, sometimes as a stand-in for orthodontics.

paras: The dentist usually removes a thin layer of enamel (the amount varies, and some systems use little or none), takes an impression or digital scan, and bonds a veneer made in a lab or chairside. The change is visible straight away. Some people combine the work with a trip to Turkey, where multi-tooth packages are offered.

Reported complications include chipping, debonding, marginal staining, sensitivity and decay. Preparation that exposes dentin is associated with lower success rates, and enamel lost in preparation does not regrow. Critics cited by Wikipedia describe overuse on healthy teeth as instant orthodontics.

angle.text: Shells bonded over your teeth unify colour, shape and alignment for a whiter, straighter-looking smile, visible straight away. Reviews report high survival over about a decade, and preparation can remove enamel.

lead: A dental veneer is a layer of material, most often dental porcelain or composite resin, bonded to the front surface of a tooth to change its colour, shape, size or apparent position. [1] For appearance, this is the most direct route dentistry offers to a whiter, more even, better-proportioned smile: a set of veneers can mask stains that whitening does not shift, close small gaps, lengthen worn or short teeth and even out asymmetry in a single course of treatment. [1][2] Laminate veneers are mostly cosmetic and cover only the facial surface, while full veneer crowns cover all coronal surfaces. [1]

Multi-tooth cosmetic makeovers are commonly called 'Hollywood smile' treatments, and 'Turkey teeth' has become a nickname for veneers or crowns obtained at lower prices at dental clinics in Turkey, where the work is offered in cities such as Istanbul, Ankara and Antalya. [1][3] Wikipedia reports that treatment in Turkey is described in one cited source as up to 70% cheaper than in the US or UK, a figure that comes from a commercial dental site. [1]

The clinical literature on ceramic laminate veneers is substantial. A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of 29 studies reported pooled survival of about 96% for feldspathic, 94% for leucite-reinforced and 97% for lithium disilicate veneers at around 10 years, with technical complications more frequent for feldspathic ceramics. [4] A 2024 narrative review of 55 studies similarly found satisfactory survival and success for these ceramics, with dentin exposure lowering success. [5] Reviews and dental commentators also stress that the amount of tooth removed, the bonding protocol and the dentist's planning shape both the look and the lifespan of the result. [5][6][2]

In looksmaxxing communities veneers are described as a high-impact change to facial appearance, and posters discuss dental work as part of surgery trips to Turkey alongside hair transplants, rhinoplasty and other procedures. [7][8][9] Other threads argue about the risks of having work done abroad. [10] The research literature covers the clinical performance of veneers; no studies were identified on the 'Turkey teeth' practice as a defined phenomenon.

paras: Veneers are used on discoloured teeth that do not respond to whitening, on teeth with enamel defects such as hypoplasia or fluorosis, on worn or chipped teeth, on small gaps and on irregular shape or length. Wikipedia lists these among the accepted indications, along with 'dark triangles' left by gum recession. [1] Wikipedia notes that composite temporaries can be placed while final veneers are made, acting as a trial run for eating, speech and appearance. [1]

Because a laminate veneer covers only the visible face of the tooth, treatment is usually aimed at the front teeth that show when a person smiles, and Wikipedia describes the multi-tooth version as a 'Hollywood' makeover of several upper teeth. [1]

Composite veneers can be built directly on the tooth, or made outside the mouth and bonded; porcelain veneers are made indirectly. [1][11] Wikipedia says composite lasts about four years and porcelain is more durable and stains less, although other sources report longer composite survival. [1] A review of the direct-indirect composite technique describes advantages such as try-in before luting and improved marginal adaptation. [11]

Wikipedia describes four classic porcelain-laminate preparation outlines (window, feather, bevel and incisal overlap) and a 2012 classification system that sorts veneers by coverage, contact-point involvement, production method and material. [1] 'No-prep' or ultra-thin veneers, which require little or no tooth reduction, are mentioned in the same article, which notes the claim needs stronger sourcing. [1]

A review of anterior veneer restorations argued that the evidence supporting some newer materials does not justify their use over established techniques, and that direct composite veneers remain widely used and are usually more affordable than indirect ones. [6] Digital design and CAD/CAM manufacture are increasingly used, and prefabricated composite shells and 3D-printed composite veneers are being studied. [12][13][14][15]

For indirect veneers the dentist usually removes a thin layer of enamel, takes an impression or scan, fits a temporary and later bonds the finished shell. [1][2] A 2018 update on porcelain veneers emphasises keeping the preparation boundaries within enamel, and the 2024 review reports that etching ceramic with hydrofluoric acid and priming with silane improves clinical outcomes. [2][5]

Bonding to enamel performs better than bonding to dentin; the technique of immediate dentin sealing was proposed to improve bonding where dentin is exposed during preparation. [5][16] A review of resin bonding and high-strength ceramics likewise addresses how the adhesive step affects longevity. [17]

Wikipedia credits California dentist Charles Pincus with inventing veneers in 1928 for a film shoot, where they changed the look of actors' teeth temporarily, and with making acrylic veneers held by denture adhesive in 1937. [1] Michael Buonocore's work on acid etching in 1959 and the early-1980s demonstration by Simonsen and Calamia that porcelain could be etched with hydrofluoric acid and bonded with resin led to veneers that could be attached to enamel permanently. [1]

Wikipedia notes later fabrication techniques described by Calamia and Horn in 1983 and clinical follow-ups through the 1990s. [1] A 2000 literature review examined the parameters for long-term success, and a 2018 update discussed preparation designs and glass-ceramic materials. [2][18]

A 2025 meta-analysis (29 studies, minimum one-year follow-up) found no difference in survival between feldspathic, leucite-reinforced and lithium disilicate veneers, with complication rates at about 10 years of roughly 41%, 30% and 6% for technical events respectively; zirconia veneers showed full survival but only 2.6 years of data. [4] A 2024 review reported that none of 55 studies met criteria for zirconia laminate veneers. [5]

A randomized split-mouth trial placed 24 indirect resin composite and 24 ceramic laminate veneers on maxillary anterior teeth and followed them for up to 10 years, and a randomized trial compared CAD/CAM lithium disilicate veneers with heat-pressed ones. [19][20] A systematic review of anterior composite restorations has examined long-term survival and reasons for failure. [21] Registered trials include studies of prefabricated versus 3D-printed composite veneers, a six-year follow-up of prefabricated composite veneers, zirconia laminate veneers, and cementation techniques. [14][15][22][23]
Laboratory work includes measurement of tooth structure removed by different preparation designs, where veneer preparations were found less invasive than complete-coverage crown preparations. [24]

Turkey is a major destination for medical tourism; Wikipedia reports that it draws large numbers of foreign patients each year, that a regulation on international health tourism took effect in July 2017 and that a state body to promote and regulate the sector was set up in 2019. [3] Veneers, crowns and implants are among the dental services offered in Istanbul, Ankara and Antalya. [3]

Medical-tourism reviews list general concerns that apply to any treatment abroad: varying aftercare, difficulty obtaining follow-up or insurance cover at home, and limited recourse if something goes wrong. [3] Critics of mass multi-tooth packages, as reported by Wikipedia, say veneers or crowns are sometimes placed on healthy teeth that could have been treated less invasively, a pattern one Canadian dentist called 'instant orthodontics'. [1] No outcome studies of Turkish veneer packages were identified.
Discussion on looksmax.org includes both trip announcements and a thread whose title argues against having procedures done in Turkey. [7][10]

Wikipedia lists contraindications including poor oral hygiene, gum disease, grinding and unrealistic expectations, and notes that preparation can cause sensitivity and decay and that veneers can fail or need replacement. [1] It also reports that inexperienced preparation can remove a substantial share of the tooth surface and that the long-term upkeep cost can be considerable. [1]

Reviews report that bonding to dentin gives poorer results than bonding to enamel, and that immediate dentin sealing is used to improve bonding in indirect restorations. [5][16] Preparation designs vary from conservative to extensive, and the 2002 study of tooth structure removal reported large differences between designs. [24] Enamel removed in preparation does not grow back, so a prepared tooth generally needs a restoration for life, a point reviews of minimal-intervention approaches build on. [6]

On looksmax.org, users discuss veneers as improving apparent health and facial harmony; one thread's replies say veneers make a face look healthier. [9] One thread is titled as a high-effort 'guide' to veneers. [25] Another poster asks about having veneers or crowns made in Turkey to address an underbite. [8] A forum post announcing a Turkey trip lists veneers among about a dozen procedures with a stated cost of about $15,000, and the same poster says they travelled to Turkey earlier in the year for a hair transplant, rhinoplasty and other work. [7]

In these communities veneers sit in the same conversation as orthodontics, jaw surgery and 'hardmaxxing', and are often discussed as a relatively accessible change compared with skeletal surgery. [7][8][25]

lore.intro: Veneers come up on looksmax.org as a smile upgrade, as a possible substitute for orthodontics, and as one part of multi-procedure trips to Turkey. [7][8][9] Threads also debate the risks of treatment abroad. [10]
